title: Ricc. de Mutiliana (Forli) to Gianfrancesco Gonzaga, 6 Nov 1428, Archivio di Stato di Mantova (DECODE R1854 image 3)

steps.what: Fetched R1854 (5 images), the R1853 register (14 images) and DECODE metadata with the saved cookie.
Read the R1853 register keys (Malatesta keys on f. 1, 1406-1419 keys): none match the 1428-30 letters.
Subagent read P3's faint interlinear gloss (about two-thirds legible) and the three name codes.
Subagent transcribed P3's 894 cipher signs with gloss letters attached.
P3 key from the gloss (30 sign values) plus rare signs from context; whole letter deciphered from the signs.
Split from the R1854 entry under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the record's four letters use four ciphers; image 3 is this entry. 869 of 894 signs read as sense (0.972, 5 Oct 2026 count).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 875 tokens, 50 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.145 per letter; random keys -4.343 (z 6.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.864 (mean -2.909, z 22.7); annealer on the real text -2.267. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.145; polyphony 0.0; 19 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.267

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was taken from the contemporary interlinear gloss over the signs (30 sign values, each attested 2-56 times; about two-thirds of the gloss legible), rare signs fixed from context, and every run deciphered from its signs rather than from the faint gloss.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_p3.md: 869 of 894 cipher signs (ct_p3.txt, measured) read as sense; re-counted 5 Oct 2026.

gaps.detail: no gloss over them, two and one occurrences

outcome.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 from the four-letter R1854 entry. The method (adjacent plaintext rather than existing decipherment) is an assumption for George Lasry's review: the gloss is partial and the key was applied to the signs.

credits.note: interlinear decipherment of the letter, the key source

prior.where: contemporary letter-by-letter interlinear decipherment on the letter, faint, about two-thirds legible
